Backing: "O'Keeffe exhibition at . . . / 1930. / . . . Abstraction by Georgia O'Keeffe – 1930." (Alfred Stieglitz, Label: handwritten, "An American Place' / 509 Madison Ave —Room 1710 / (S.E. corner 53rd St) — New York", red ink) 
(Source: Lynes, 1999)

cr_data.provenance: (An American Place, New York, NY); Mary C. Wheelwright, Alcalde, New Mexico, 1932; Maria Chabot, Alcalde, New Mexico, gift, 1944; Ann C. Shearer, Tiburon, California, 1977; (Doris Bry, New York, NY); Private collection, New York, NY, 1979 (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "1930. Sold to Miss Mary Wheelwright." Abiquiú Notebooks notes inscription and indicates, "Bought from American Place in 1930." 1932 purchase date on basis of Stieglitz–O'Keeffe correspondence. Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate no. 2 in 1930 New York (An American Place) exhibition. Whitney Archive indicates as "Abstraction – Seaweed." Abiquiú Notebooks indicates as "Abstraction." The painting is not included on the exhibition checklist as *Abstraction – Seaweed*, and the two abstractions that are included on the checklist (nos. 1 and 2) are pictured in 1930 New York (An American Place) Stieglitz installation photographs, see cat. nos. 700, 701. If this painting was exhibited in 1930, it was not included on the checklist. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.notes: Source of title: Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks, backing inscription.
titles.title: Abstraction

description: Layers of billowing white and gray forms that resemble draped fabric spread across the composition. In the lower part of the composition, small green form that resembles a pine branch is visible between the folds.
